project.name: rendering/pathtracing/async_shader_compilation
project.about: If `true`, path tracing ray hit shaders are compiled asynchronously in the background.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/debug_heatmap_max_ticks
project.about: Elapsed device clock ticks mapped to purple in `Environment.RT_DEBUG_TIMING_HEATMAP`.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/debug_heatmap_opacity
project.about: Opacity of `Environment.RT_DEBUG_TIMING_HEATMAP`, applied after denoising and tone mapping.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/decals
project.about: Which path vertices the path tracer projects Decals onto.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/deformed_mesh_cache_ttl_frames
project.about: Number of frames a skinned or vertex-displaced deformed-mesh BLAS is kept alive in the path tracer cache after its last visible frame.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_blas_build_triangle_budget
project.about: Maximum number of triangles in full BLAS builds of dynamic geometry (GPU particles, camera-facing MultiMeshes) per frame, shared by all viewports.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_blas_max_operations
project.about: Maximum number of BLAS builds plus refits of dynamic geometry per frame, shared by all viewports.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_blas_update_triangle_budget
project.about: Maximum number of triangles in BLAS refits of dynamic geometry per frame, shared by all viewports.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_max_stale_frames
project.about: Dynamic geometry that has not been updated for this many frames is updated even when the visibility estimate says it can wait.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_offscreen_size_weight
project.about: Priority weight of dynamic geometry outside the camera frustum, which only reflections, refractions and shadows can see.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/dynamic_rebuild_interval_frames
project.about: One in this many BLAS updates of dynamic geometry is a full rebuild instead of a refit, restoring the BVH quality that refits slowly lose as particles spread.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/emissive_lights
project.about: The path tracer samples emissive surfaces (opaque StandardMaterial3D with emission, up to 1024 a frame, the strongest at the camera) as lights: each shaded point gets a light sample on one of them, weighed against bounce rays by multiple importance sampling.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/hair
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer scatters light off surfaces with `BaseMaterial3D.hair_enabled` as hair fibres do (Chiang, Bitterli, Tappan and Burley, "A Practical and Controllable Hair and Fur Model for Production Path Tracing", 2016): a white highlight shifted towards the roots, light passing through the fibres, a coloured second highlight and all longer paths, with lights, bounce rays and emissive surfaces all sampled through it.
project.title: Hair

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/indirect_reuse
project.about: Where a camera ray's first hit sends its first bounce through the diffuse lobe, that bounce is kept per pixel (ReSTIR GI: Ouyang et al.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/light_reuse
project.about: Where a camera ray first hits a surface, the positional light it picks is kept per pixel (ReSTIR DI: spatiotemporal reservoir resampling, Bitterli et al.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/light_visibility_memory
project.about: The path tracer remembers, for each small region of the scene, which lights recently lit it and how often each light's samples were blocked or fell on the surface's unlit side.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/back_lighting
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer passes light through surfaces with back lighting (`BaseMaterial3D.backlight_enabled`, or `BACKLIGHT` in a shader), such as leaves, paper, curtains and lampshades.
project.title: Materials

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/caustics
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer draws water caustics from the first DirectionalLight3D: the bright, moving lines a rippled surface gathers sunlight into on the floor below it.
project.title: Water

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/caustics_area
project.about: Width in metres of the square that gets `rendering/pathtracing/caustics`, centred on the surface at the middle of the screen (at least half its width ahead of the camera).

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/caustics_cascades
project.about: How many caustics maps cover the water, as shadow cascades do: each is 4 times wider than the one before around the same centre (`rendering/pathtracing/caustics_area`, then 4 and 16 times it: 16, 64 and 256 m by default).
project.title: Water

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/clearcoat
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer traces the clear coat of materials (`BaseMaterial3D.clearcoat_enabled`, or `CLEARCOAT` in a shader) as the rasterizer shades it: a thin glossy dielectric layer over the surface, reflecting about 4% of light head-on and more at grazing angles, on the mesh's normal without the normal map.
project.title: Materials

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/cull_max_distance
project.about: Distance in meters past which geometry outside the camera's view is left out of path tracing, so it casts no shadows or reflections and bounces no light.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/cull_min_size
project.about: Angular radius in degrees under which an object outside the camera's view is left out of path tracing: its bounding sphere's radius over its distance from the camera, so small objects drop out sooner than large ones.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/mesh_lod
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer traces each static mesh surface at the level of detail the rasterizer would draw it at, using the mesh's LODs (generated on import) and `rendering/mesh_lod/lod_change/threshold_pixels`.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/persistent_instances
project.about: If `true`, each traced mesh instance keeps its acceleration-structure instances and geometry data from frame to frame, and only instances that changed (moved, changed material, mesh, layers or visibility) are written again.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transmission
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer traces light through surfaces with `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_enabled` as thin glass: rays and shadows pass straight through, tinted by the albedo, less the light the surface reflects, and blurred by roughness.
project.title: Materials

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/refraction
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer refracts light into and out of surfaces with `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_enabled` and `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_thin_walled` off, such as water or a glass block: rays bend by `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_ior`, with total internal reflection, and every ray inside is absorbed by `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_attenuation_color` and `BaseMaterial3D.transmission_attenuation_distance` (Beer-Lambert), so deep water darkens and tints by depth.
project.title: Water

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/radiance_cache
project.about: The path tracer learns, in cells around the camera, how much light rough surfaces send back, their own lighting and further bounces together.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/relative_origin_grid
project.about: Size in meters of the grid the path tracer's origin snaps to.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/simulated_gas
project.about: The path tracer traces simulated gas (smoke and fire from the PhysX module's Flow node) as a participating medium: light scatters inside it, it casts soft shadows, it shows in reflections, and fire emits light into the scene.
project.title: Physics (PhysX 5)

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/subsurface_scattering
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer traces subsurface scattering (`BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_enabled`, or `SSS_STRENGTH` in a shader) as light wandering inside the mesh: a bounce enters the surface, takes a random walk through a medium whose colour after many scattering events is the albedo and whose radius is `rendering/pathtracing/subsurface_scattering_scale` times the strength, and leaves where it next meets the surface, where lights are sampled.
project.title: Materials

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/subsurface_scattering_scale
project.about: Radius in metres that light travels under a surface with `rendering/pathtracing/subsurface_scattering` at a subsurface strength of `1.0`; the strength scales it.
project.title: Materials

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/max_decals
project.about: Maximum number of Decals the path tracer considers per frame, from `0` to `65536`.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/max_transparency_layers
project.about: Maximum number of transparent layers the path tracer peels on primary (camera) segments, from `0` to `64`.
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/max_transparency_layers_indirect
project.about: Maximum number of transparent layers the path tracer peels on non-singular (diffuse and glossy) bounce segments, from `0` to `64`.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/max_transparency_layers_reflection
project.about: Maximum number of transparent layers the path tracer peels on singular (mirror) reflection chains after the camera segment, from `0` to `64`.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/multimesh_blas_cache_ttl_frames
project.about: Number of frames a merged MultiMesh BLAS is kept alive in the path tracer cache after its last visible frame.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/multimesh_cache_cpu_transforms
project.about: When enabled, setting `MultiMesh.buffer` keeps a CPU-side mirror of the instance transform data in sync with the GPU buffer.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/linear_swept_spheres
project.about: If `true`, on a device with linear swept spheres (Vulkan `VK_NV_ray_tracing_linear_swept_spheres`, hardware hair primitives) the path tracer traces strand hair (`render_mode hair_strands` on a mesh of two crossed strips per strand point, as PhysXHair3D draws it) as round tubes between the strand points, one primitive per segment instead of four triangles, and shades each fibre from where the ray meets it across its width.
project.title: Hair

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/multimesh_merged_blas_max_triangles
project.about: Maximum total triangle count (`instance_count * triangles_per_surface`) for a MultiMesh surface to use a single merged BLAS in the path tracer.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/opacity_micromap_max_level
project.about: The finest subdivision level of an opacity micromap triangle (4^level micro-triangles), also capped by the device.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/opacity_micromap_scale
project.about: The alpha texels one opacity micromap micro-triangle covers; a triangle's level follows its area in texels.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/opacity_micromaps
project.about: If `true`, static surfaces whose StandardMaterial3D uses alpha scissor get an opacity micromap (Vulkan `VK_EXT_opacity_micromap`), baked on the GPU from the material's albedo alpha the first time they are traced.
project.title: Open worlds

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/parallel_planning
project.about: If `true`, the path tracer plans its per-frame instance records on the worker thread pool once a viewport has at least 256 instances.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparency_dominant_layer_alpha
project.about: Minimum alpha the nearest transparent layer needs to become the pixel's dominant surface in the path tracer.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparency_indirect_fade
project.about: Distance in meters over which transparent layers fade out before reaching `rendering/pathtracing/transparency_indirect_range`.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparency_indirect_range
project.about: Maximum distance in meters that indirect (bounce) ray segments trace for transparent surfaces.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparency_max_bounce
project.about: Last bounce index at which the path tracer performs transparency handling.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transmission_bounces
project.about: Extra path segments for transmission (glass, ice, water, at any roughness).
project.title: Lighting

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/use_shader_execution_reordering
project.about: If `true`, enables NVIDIA Shader Execution Reordering in the path tracer.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparency_at_output_size
project.about: Under DLSS Ray Reconstruction, transparent surfaces (particles, glass, rain) are drawn into a layer of their own at the internal resolution and laid over Ray Reconstruction's output.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/bounce
project.about: If `true`, each cell of the path tracer's light cache for transparents (see `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/enabled`) also traces one ray a frame in a random direction: the sky and the light bounced off the traced scene (a lit wall, a neon sign) reach particles and transparents.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/enabled
project.about: If `true`, transparent surfaces and particles (rain, splashes, smoke, glass) are lit by the path tracer while it is on: a camera-aligned grid of cells (the internal size over 8 across, 64 slices from `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/near` to `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/far`) is refreshed by the trace every frame, each cell taking one omni or spot light from the light grid, picked by its contribution, and every directional light, each through a shadow ray, and the sky and one bounce (see `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/bounce`), blended over the frames.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/far
project.about: The view distance, in meters, where the path tracer's light cache for transparents ends (see `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/enabled`).

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/near
project.about: The view distance, in meters, where the path tracer's light cache for transparents begins (see `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/far`).

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/particle_anisotropy
project.about: How much light particles scatter forward under the path tracer's light cache for transparents (see `rendering/pathtracing/transparent_lighting/enabled`).

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/use_simple_shadows
project.about: If `true`, shadow rays use Ray Queries instead of fully traced rays.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/vertex_capture_mode
project.about: Controls which surfaces the path tracer vertex-captures: it runs the material's raster `vertex()` function and traces the resulting geometry, so custom vertex displacement, hand-written `MODELVIEW_MATRIX` billboards and particle trails match the rasterized image.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/volumetric_fog_positional_shadow_rays
project.about: Maximum number of shadow rays traced per volumetric fog froxel for shadowed OmniLight3Ds and SpotLight3Ds when path tracing.

project.name: rendering/pathtracing/volumetric_fog_shadows
project.about: If `true`, volumetric fog traces ray query shadows for shadowed lights when path tracing.

project.name: rendering/streamline/dlss_preset
project.about: The default NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution preset to use.

project.name: rendering/streamline/dlss_ray_reconstruction_preset
project.about: The default NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction preset to use.
project.title: DLSS Ray Reconstruction

project.name: rendering/streamline/reflex_frame_limit_us
project.about: If not `0`, enables NVIDIA Reflex Frame Rate Limiter, which intelligently reduces framerate whilst keeping latency as low as possible.

project.name: rendering/streamline/reflex_mode
project.about: If `1`, enables NVIDIA Reflex, which reduces latency by rendering just before vertical sync.

project.name: rendering/streamline/streamline_imgui
project.about: If `1`, enables Streamline ImgUI Plugin.

project.name: rendering/streamline/streamline_log
project.about: If `1`, enables Streamline Logging.

environment.name: pathtracing_debug_mode
environment.about: Selects a debug visualization channel to display instead of the final path-traced image.

environment.name: pathtracing_denoiser
environment.about: The denoiser used to reduce noise in the path-traced image.

environment.name: pathtracing_enabled
environment.about: If `true`, enables hardware-accelerated path tracing for this environment.

environment.name: pathtracing_max_bounces
environment.about: Maximum number of times a ray is allowed to bounce off surfaces before it is terminated.

environment.name: pathtracing_samples_per_pixel
environment.about: Number of ray samples cast per pixel per frame.

environment.name: pathtracing_sky_shader_enabled
environment.about: If `true`, the sky shader is evaluated per-pixel into a screen-space buffer and sampled directly by camera rays, so the path-traced background matches the rasterized sky exactly.
environment.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: 4096 lights
features.what: camera-following light grid with resampled importance sampling.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Light visibility memory
features.what: hidden lights stop taking samples.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Radiance cache
features.what: bounces end on cached light.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Transmission bounces
features.what: glass, ice and water get their own bounce budget; matches 6 bounces in about 70% of the time, so icicles under an eave no longer go dark at the default 3.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Light reuse
features.what: ReSTIR DI reuses light samples across pixels and frames.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Indirect light reuse
features.what: ReSTIR GI; rooms and shade lit by bounced light are far less noisy at the same samples.
features.title: Lighting

features.name: Back lighting
features.what: light through leaves, paper and curtains, with coloured shadows; back light texture.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Transmission
features.what: thin glass, tinted and blurred by roughness, with tinted shadows; transmission texture; `TRANSMISSION` in shaders; glTF `KHR_materials_transmission`.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Raster refraction through solids
features.what: raster refraction leaves a solid through its far side, not just the front face.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Clearcoat
features.what: matches raster, with traced coat reflections; coat texture.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Subsurface scattering
features.what: random walk inside closed meshes; skin, wax and marble soften and thin parts glow when backlit.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Wet surfaces
features.what: porous surfaces darken and turn glossier as the weather map gets wet, raster and path traced; `get_wetness_shader_code()` for ShaderMaterials.
features.title: Materials

features.name: Refraction
features.what: water and glass blocks bend light by their IOR, with total internal reflection and depth tint; glTF `KHR_materials_volume`, `KHR_materials_ior`.
features.title: Water

features.name: Murky water
features.what: scattering media; `IOR`, `ABSORPTION` and `SCATTERING` in shaders; glTF `KHR_materials_scatter` draft.
features.title: Water

features.name: Caustics
features.what: sunlight lines under rippled water.
features.title: Water

features.name: Caustic cascades
features.what: sun caustics out to 256 m, near lines unchanged.
features.title: Water

features.name: Path-traced ocean
features.what: waves refract, tint and scatter, with caustics on the seabed.
features.title: Water

features.name: Ocean swell
features.what: up to four wave layers give long swell under the chop without visible tiling, whitecaps where they add up, on a shallow-water (TMA) spectrum; set `depth` to the real depth for open sea (the 3 m default damps long waves).
features.title: Water

features.name: Measured wave spreading
features.what: Donelan-Banner spreading as Horvath (2015) fits it, with swell; slopes at 14 m/s match Cox and Munk's measurements.
features.title: Water

features.name: Whitecaps by wind speed
features.what: whitecap cover follows the wind speed as measured at sea (Monahan 1980), whatever the wave settings.
features.title: Water

features.name: Lake ripples
features.what: on short fetches the wave grid gets finer, up to 256 points, so lakes keep their short wind ripples and sun glitter; open sea is unchanged.
features.title: Water

features.name: Raster reflections
features.what: raster sea and rivers reflect the sky and the sun's glitter by the exact Fresnel term, matching the path tracer; raster waterfalls, white water, sea foam and wet sand take the scene's shadows, sky light and cloud shadows; the water's own colour is lit by sun and sky, so the sea darkens at dusk.
features.title: Water

features.name: Boat wakes
features.what: waves stepped with deep-water dispersion in Fourier space form the Kelvin pattern, a 19.5 degree wedge of transverse and diverging waves.
features.title: Water

features.name: Shore waves
features.what: swell turns with the seabed, grows in the shallows, breaks and runs up the sand (Stockdon run-up).
features.title: Water

features.name: Wave groups
features.what: shore waves arrive in sets with their own Rayleigh heights, so each breaks at its own place.
features.title: Water

features.name: Plunging breakers
features.what: the crest throws a sheet of water that lands ahead and sinks into the bore, with spray where it is thin and where it lands.
features.title: Water

features.name: Currents
features.what: flow round rocks and along shores carries waves, foam and floating objects.
features.title: Water

features.name: Live flow
features.what: near the player, rocks and banks shed wakes and eddies.
features.title: Water

features.name: White water
features.what: foam in fast water, trailing rocks and drifting downstream.
features.title: Water

features.name: Rivers
features.what: drawn as a curve; finds its depth and never runs uphill.
features.title: Water

features.name: Contact waterfalls
features.what: water that clings to steep rock, as wide as its flow, clear at the lip and white below the inception point, with soft wandering edges, wet rock beside it and spray off ledges. Thin falls over stepped rock run ledge to ledge as threads with wet rock between them, as their flow sets (`rock_step`); big flows stay fully covered.
features.title: Water

features.name: Plunging waterfalls
features.what: tall falls break up into a falling column of clumps slowed by the air, inside a spray veil and soft mist.
features.title: Water

features.name: Faster flow bakes
features.what: multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradients bake the flow 7 to 10 times faster than SOR.
features.title: Water

features.name: Camera under water
features.what: fog, scattering, Snell's window, image split at the water line.
features.title: Water

features.name: Fibre shading
features.what: Chiang hair model under path tracing, melanin colour, on shells, cards and strands; mask for single-material characters.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Raster hair shading
features.what: Marschner model as Unreal evaluates it, with multiple scattering and light through the strands in shadow maps, so backlit hair glows.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Deep opacity shadows
features.what: raster strands shadow themselves in depth, calibrated against the path tracer; omni and spot lights too (`deep_shadow_local_lights`).
features.title: Hair

features.name: Hair shadows
features.what: raster strand hair casts shadows on the face, body and ground.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Custom hair shaders
features.what: `HAIR`, `HAIR_ABSORPTION`, `HAIR_ROUGHNESS` and `POSITIONAL_SHADOW_OFFSET` outputs; `hair_strands` and `hair_cards` render modes; `IN_PATH_TRACER` built-in.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Strand grooms
features.what: grown on a scalp mesh or loaded from a HAIR file.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Moving strand hair
features.what: AMD TressFX's simulation on GPU compute, guide and follow strands, velocity shock propagation, wind with gusts and turbulence, collision spheres.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Swept sphere strands
features.what: where the GPU traces swept spheres in hardware, strands are traced as round tubes, one primitive per segment, and shaded where the ray meets the fibre; other GPUs keep crossed strips. Not yet checked on supporting hardware.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Raster strands
features.what: blended and sorted far to near on the GPU each frame; smooth without TAA or MSAA, and the hair shadows itself.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Distance LOD
features.what: far away, fewer and wider strands with the same look; simulation and path tracing keep every strand. Straight hair is drawn through fewer points with the same look (`simplify_tolerance`).
features.title: Hair

features.name: Hair cards for crowds
features.what: distant strand hair can switch to textured cards baked from its own groom, simulating only its guides; raster only, path tracing keeps the strands.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Motion vectors for strands
features.what: TAA, FSR 2 and DLSS follow moving hair instead of smearing it; shaders get `PREVIOUS_FRAME` and `render_mode alpha_motion_vectors`.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Wet hair
features.what: strands soak in rain and dry over time, turning darker, glossier, heavier, flatter and clumped.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Snow on hair
features.what: snow from the weather settles on the top layer and windward side as small clumps, and melts into wetness.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Grey and sun-bleached hair
features.what: single grey strands mixed through the hair, and lengths lighter and warmer toward the tips.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Body collision
features.what: strands collide with a body mesh, skinned or not, through a distance field built on the GPU every frame.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Hair on cloth
features.what: strands rest on simulated cloth such as a collar or hood, lying over it as it moves.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Strand-strand collision
features.what: guide strands no longer pass through each other, with friction.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Hair volume
features.what: strands push and drag on each other through a density grid, so hair keeps its volume.
features.title: Hair

features.name: Mountain generation
features.what: raises ranges from an uplift map, Path3D ranges and noise, then erodes them to equilibrium with stream power erosion; branching gullies come from an erosion filter computed per point, so tiles join exactly; on crests gullies keep part of their depth and a ridged noise adds irregular pinnacles; the same for a seed; writes into Terrain3D or a HeightMapShape3D.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Coarse-to-fine erosion
features.what: about 3.7 times faster at 4 m cells, with the same relief.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Tile erosion
features.what: droplet hydraulic and thermal erosion in seamless overlapping tiles.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Material detail
features.what: erosion detail below the vertex spacing in the terrain material; path tracing keeps it.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Rock layers and waterfalls
features.what: hard and soft bands that rivers cut into caprock waterfalls.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Glacial erosion
features.what: ice ages alternate with the rivers and carve troughs, cirques and basins that become lakes. With rock quality varied (`glacial_rock_variation`, `glacial_rock_scale`, off by default) the ice digs its own basins and bars, so tarns and chains of lakes form with no markers. Glaciers from beyond the map edge flow in with their rivers and carve the main valley's trough and lakes (`glacial_inflow_balance`, m/yr, 0 = off). A coarser ice grid (`glacial_coarse_cell`) is about 3 times faster, with similar but not identical terrain.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Moraines
features.what: debris carried down the last glaciers builds ridges at their margins that dam lakes. Till draws as soil with stones through it, the stones kept above the grass.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Ice-worn rock
features.what: faces toward the old ice flow are smoothed, faces away are stepped, with striations.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Cliff ledges
features.what: rock beds of uneven thickness step faces steeper than 40 degrees into ledges.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Scree
features.what: rock walls shed aprons and cones at their feet, kept out of lakes and river floors. Scree draws as bare blocks.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Fallen blocks
features.what: blocks shed by cliffs rest below them, the largest furthest out.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: River deposition
features.what: rivers drop sediment where they slow (Yuan et al. 2019), building flat alluvial valley floors; solved exactly per step along the river tree, at about half the earlier cost.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Meandering rivers
features.what: bends grow and migrate across flat valley floors; cut-off loops leave oxbows that silt up, and the river water follows the new course.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Rivers fed by rain and snowmelt
features.what: a monthly water balance from the climate sets each river's flow, month by month.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: River network
features.what: rivers with widths and discharges, made into joined `PhysXRiver3D` paths.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: River sites
features.what: position, discharge, catchment, drop and run along every river, for placing lakes and falls.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Waterfall records
features.what: each fall's type, lip, face profiles, tiers, power, impact speed and plunge pool, for water effects.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Plunge pools and gorges
features.what: falls of 4 m or more scour a pool that holds water, and lips over hard rock wear back upstream into slot gorges.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Spray map
features.what: where fall spray keeps the ground wet, from each fall's power and distance.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Coast and lakes
features.what: sea with a Dean-profile seabed and beaches; lakes behind natural dams or rock lips that spill as waterfalls; builds the sea and lake surfaces, and rivers end in them.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Geology maps
features.what: soil, bare rock and scree from the erosion run.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Climate maps
features.what: temperature, orographic rain and rain shadows, snow share, aridity, winter and annual sunlight with terrain shadows, and wind exposure.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Terrain data maps
features.what: bakes slope, curvature, water flow, wetness, water depth and distance to water around a point, for placing plants and for materials; a 512 map bakes once in about 0.2 s.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Ground material
features.what: rock, scree, soil, alluvium and sand from the generator's geology, height-blended, biplanar cliffs, erosion detail, wetness and snow.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Sky occlusion
features.what: raster ground is lit only by the sky its hills leave open, from a horizon bake and the live sky, matching path tracing at dusk.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Rock detail
features.what: steep rock shows bedding planes and joints, and scree and till show loose stones, with no textures and no stretching on any face.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Cliff relief
features.what: steep faces near the camera are refined without cracks and displaced into real bed ledges and joint blocks, path traced too.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Far blend
features.what: far ground takes the colour of the plant cover map.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Landscape3D
features.what: heightfield ground from a TerrainGenerator3D or a height image, as chunk meshes with crack-free LODs and one BLAS per chunk level, so nothing rebuilds while the camera moves. Heights stream in coarse first and chunk meshes build on worker threads (`stream_heights`); baked heights load 4 km at 1 m in under a second.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Landscape3D collision
features.what: full-detail heightfield tiles follow the player and match the drawn triangles.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Footprints in ground
features.what: prints in sand, soil, mud and leaf litter; moisture from the weather map, walls slump to the angle of repose.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Terrain deformation
features.what: non-destructive height brushes (rivers, craters, plots) over Terrain3D or a height map; moving a brush restores the ground.
features.title: Terrain

features.name: Plant placement
features.what: places species by spacing, footprint and rules on slope, wetness and distance to water over a `TerrainDataMap3D`; evenly spread, the same for a seed. 12,899 plants over 256 m place once in about 45 ms, then draw as ordinary MultiMeshes.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Streamed placement
features.what: tiles are placed on worker threads around the camera, identical to a full placement; 2 to 3 ms of main-thread time a frame through 1 km of oak wood.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Placement by geology
features.what: plants follow the generated soil, rock and scree; trees stay off bare rock and thin soil, grass thins on rock.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Placement by climate
features.what: species by temperature, winter frost, rain, aridity and sunlight.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Density masks
features.what: a painted texture thins or clears any species per channel, for clearings and paths.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Waterfall spray
features.what: plants keep out of the soaked ground in a waterfall's spray zone, where only mosses grow.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Plant cover map
features.what: a colour map of the plant cover baked from the planting rules, for distant terrain.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Canopy shade
features.what: understorey placed by the shade of placed crowns; crowns feed the weather's canopy map.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Grass
features.what: blades grow round the camera in clumps, follow `TerrainDataMap3D` rules, thin with distance, bend in the `WeatherMap3D` wind (each blade answers gusts at its own frequency, about 2 Hz, and the sway rolls downwind as waves) and darken in rain; near tall grass at 120 blades per m²; the sward darkens inside from its leaf area (raster AO) and casts its blades' true shadow; path traced.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Grass on the GPU
features.what: grass tiles are filled in compute, about 40% less main-thread cost per tile.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Grass edge fade
features.what: blades thin and shrink across the outer band of the grass radius, and the ground takes their colour beyond (measured from a render of the blades, so any grass look matches), so the grass has no hard edge; it thins evenly with distance by blue-noise blade ranks, with no clumps or gaps.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Far grass in sunlight
features.what: distant grass brightens looking away from the sun and darkens looking into it, measured from the blades at four sun headings.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Seasonal grass
features.what: grass browns in drought and hard cold and stays green in a mild winter, read from the season.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Layered meadow
features.what: blades vary in colour over the field and per blade, some dead from the root, with midribs and tapered tips; the ground under the grass becomes matching turf, and the sward follows the canopy shade.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Trampling
features.what: bodies lay grass down and it springs back.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Ground cover
features.what: edge-on blades widened, ground tinted under grass, clover and flower drifts.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Plant generator
features.what: meadow plants including tall flowers (knapweed, field scabious, wild carrot, common sorrel, some in seed), forest floor and wetland plants with seed variations, phyllotaxis, back-lit leaves with generated vein textures, and distance LODs that drop whole leaf cards and enlarge the rest to keep coverage (112k to 70k triangles on a heath), for `PlantSpecies.meshes`.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Plants by season
features.what: 17 flowering herbs open, go to seed and die back to standing stalks by degree days; fern croziers unroll in spring, fronds die back russet and lie flat through winter, and wood anemone dies down after flowering.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Forest floor
features.what: herbs, mosses and seedlings by the stand above (seedlings of the stand's own trees, with their leaf forms; dog-violets and herb Robert in the lighter patches), and the ground under closed canopy turns to leaf, needle or moss litter.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Plants on deadwood
features.what: ground plants keep off fallen logs, and moss, wood sorrel, seedlings and ferns grow on and along them.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Leaf drift
features.what: fallen leaves drift past the crowns into edges and clearings, farther downwind.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Wetland plants
features.what: reed, bulrush, rush and water lilies zoned by water depth, lilies floating on the surface.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Leaf wear
features.what: insect bites, uneven halves, dead tips and older leaves yellowing and browning, per leaf.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Bending
features.what: plants bend away from bodies and spring back, and lean in the wind.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Sun and shade growth
features.what: grass and ground plants take the colour and height of the light they grow in, like sun and shade leaves.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Per-stem sway
features.what: each frond, cane and stem rocks about its own base at a frequency set by its height and stiffness.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Near and far meshes
features.what: heavier meshes near the camera, crossfaded with dithering a few plants at a time.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Far thinning
features.what: plants thin out one by one in blue-noise order with distance and leave their colour on the ground beyond, with no tile pops.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Plant impostors
features.what: large plants turn into octahedral impostors past a range in raster (brambles and bracken past 15 m), while path tracing keeps the meshes; an oak wood view drops from 3.91M to 2.98M triangles.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: GPU-placed instances
features.what: MultiMesh records written by a compute shader reach culling, motion vectors and path tracing.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Instance bones
features.what: each instance is skinned from its own records, so thousands of plants bend in the wind without a Skeleton3D each; raster and path traced. 900 swaying stems: 0.30 ms render CPU, against 5.97 ms as 900 Skeleton3D.
features.title: Vegetation

features.name: Tree generator
features.what: trees and woody shrubs grow bud by bud, competing for light, so the same settings always give the same tree. 31 species from Europe and eastern North America, each with its climate, slope and soil habitat (`apply_habitat`).
features.title: Trees

features.name: Stand and open forms
features.what: trees grown in a closed stand shed their lower limbs to a long clear bole under a narrow crown; open-grown trees keep leaves down to their lower limbs.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Conifer crowns
features.what: spruce, fir, larch, pine and hemlock keep their cone, with branches to the top.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Stands
features.what: ten stand types, from beech, oak-lime, riparian alder and subalpine larch to North American northern hardwood and pine-hemlock. Each places canopy trees, trees in the gaps, saplings, shrubs under their shade and deadwood, and overlapping stands blend at their edges.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Shrubs and hedges
features.what: many-stemmed shrubs, drawn up and thin under a canopy; hedges and topiary clipped to a box.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Clearings
features.what: painted clearings and paths keep trees and shrubs out.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Branch collars
features.what: branches flare into their parent in a short collar with a bark ridge in the crotch. Limbs that would grow into thicker wood bend away or die back to it.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Bark
features.what: a procedural bark per species from six families (smooth, furrowed, plated, scaly, flaking, papery), with displaced relief on near trunks for raster and path tracing.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Bark moss
features.what: moss gathers at the foot of the stem and on the upper faces of limbs, thicker on rough bark and decayed wood, as real cushions near the camera.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Climbers
features.what: ivy up the stem, clematis hanging from the limbs or honeysuckle twining round them, swaying with the tree.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Leaf shapes
features.what: simple, lobed, palmate and compound leaves per species, with the true outline as geometry.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Needles
features.what: real needles near the camera, crossed needle sprays beyond.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Near leaf detail
features.what: lobed and compound leaves are built only for trees near the camera; further out each leaf is a simple leaf of the same area.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Seasons
features.what: leaves come out, turn and fall by species from the shared season state; larch turns gold and goes bare, evergreens stay.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Tree LODs
features.what: far levels drop thin wood and thin out leaves, enlarging the rest so leaf area holds; leaves stay geometry at every level.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Old trees
features.what: basal hollows, rot holes, woodpecker holes, burls, epicormic shoots and snapped crowns on the clear bole, listed by `get_veteran_features()`.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Deadwood
features.what: standing dead trees, snapped tops, stumps and fallen logs in the five forestry decay classes.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Fallen branches
features.what: shed limbs and sticks on the forest floor, from the stand's own trees.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Tree wind
features.what: trees sway in the weather map's wind and gusts, each limb at its own frequency.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Leaf flutter
features.what: leaves flutter and twist on their stalks in the same wind as grass and plants.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Far wind
features.what: trees move in the wind out to 1 km, with far ones posed less often and with fewer limbs.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Colliders and touch
features.what: trunks and limbs collide near the camera; characters and vehicles push branches aside, and fast bodies snap thin ones off.
features.title: Trees

features.name: Weather map
features.what: one weather state round the camera (wind, cloud cover, rain, wetness, puddles), read by every shader through global uniforms, raster and path traced.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Wind
features.what: slows near the ground (`roughness_length`); gusts follow the measured spectrum and travel with the wind.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Wind near the ground
features.what: shelter inside plant canopies and behind buildings; gust patches sweep across fields.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Season state
features.what: day length, budburst and leaf-colour sums, snow line, soil frost and moisture from the date and climate, for every system.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Storms
features.what: drift with the wind, with a rain core and a downdraft.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Lightning and thunder
features.what: strikes from storm cells at a rate set by cloud-top height, lit by their own channel under path tracing, with sharp shadows in raster too (`raster_shadow_distance`) and thunder made from the channel.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Precipitation haze
features.what: snow and rain haze the air in raster fog and the path traced medium; blowing snow is a lit layer near the ground.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Haze and cloud shadow in fog
features.what: volumetric fog takes the cloud shadow, and the weather adds haze from visibility and humidity.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Wet surfaces and puddles
features.what: fill with rain and dry by evaporation; materials with Wetness on darken and gloss up.
features.title: Weather

features.name: Followers
features.what: water waves grow with the weather's wind (`follow_weather`); cloth and hair move in it (`weather_wind`).
features.title: Weather

features.name: Sun and moon clock
features.what: date, time and place point the sun and moon lights, with moon phases (Meeus); the sun is within 0.0004 degrees of the ephemeris and sunrise within half a minute of the almanac (`docs/bench/sky --test`).
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Sky atmosphere
features.what: multiple scattering (Hillaire 2020) lit by sun and moon, with twilight, the Earth's shadow and clouds hazed to the horizon; `atmo_far_water` hazes far sea, `energy_per_lux` scales the lights.
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Cloud layer
features.what: shaped from the weather map's cover, cloud type and storms; drawn by `WeatherSkyMaterial` and seen by path traced rays (`pathtracing_sky_shader_enabled`).
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Clouds that never repeat
features.what: shape noise read at two scales with an irrational ratio.
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Cloud reprojection
features.what: clouds draw a sixteenth of their pixels each frame and reproject the rest (Nubis), still full resolution.
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Cloud shadows
features.what: the clouds' shadow is baked into the sun's projector, matching in raster and path tracing.
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Sun projector
features.what: `light_projector` works on DirectionalLight3D (`projector_size`, `projector_offset`), raster and path traced.
features.title: Sky and clouds

features.name: Snow cover
features.what: a snowpack from the weather map, with snowfall, settling, melt, sliding off steep slopes and wind drift.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Snowpack on a worker thread
features.what: snowpack updates run off the main thread and swap in when done, so the frame never waits; main-thread share per update about 6 ms down to about 1 ms.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Snow climate
features.what: bakes a winter over the whole terrain from the terrain's climate recipe and precipitation map, with snow lines, shaded faces that keep their snow and loaded lee slopes; the cover carries it on with the weather and draws it far away.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Fine detail kept in the wide snow map
features.what: drifts, slides and melt worked out near the camera are written back to the wide snowpack, so they are still there when the camera leaves and returns.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Shelter
features.what: ground under roofs and overhangs stays bare; tree crowns hold snow and unload it later.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Wind moves lying snow
features.what: windward shoulders and crests are scoured and the lee fills with wind-packed snow.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Melt-freeze crusts
features.what: a thawed surface refreezes into a crust that hardens each cycle; boots break thin ones into tipped pieces and stand on hard ones.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Snow on materials
features.what: surfaces are covered from the snowpack, flattest facets first, raster and path traced; `get_snow_shader_code()` for ShaderMaterials.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Deep snow
features.what: deep snow as geometry with prints and tracks; bodies sink by weight (Bekker) and rest in their own tracks; tracks refill with new snow and wind; print edges stay clean at fine deform resolutions, with pushed-aside snow sliding at its repose angle.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Deep snow on the GPU
features.what: pressing, slumping and refilling run in compute shaders, main-thread cost 1.5 ms down to 0.04 ms with the same prints; the CPU path stays for Compatibility.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Bow wave
features.what: fast bodies push the rim ahead (full at 4 m/s), leaving side berms and an end mound, mass kept; snow and ground.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Falling snow
features.what: falling and blowing snow from the weather; flake counts, sizes and fall speeds from snowfall measurements, drawn as motion streaks; roofs shelter, snow blows above the wind threshold, `get_extinction()` feeds fog.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Snowstorms
features.what: falling and blowing snow haze the air through the weather map (Pomeroy-Male suspension, 118 m visibility at 20 m/s); flakes ride turbulent eddies.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Cornices
features.what: overhangs on lee crests, with collision; milder ranges grow them too (crest wind speed-up).
features.title: Snow

features.name: Cornices crack and fall
features.what: a creeping tension crack, tumbling blocks, debris below.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Icicles
features.what: grown from roof melt water below freezing; clear ice with a hazy core.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Sparkle
features.what: dry snow glints from ice grains (its own mirror lobe, raster and path traced), lost when wet.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Exact path traced sparkle
features.what: every 2 mm ice grain is a facet hit per ray.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Sparkle in path traced reflections
features.what: snow seen in a mirror, water or a window glints too, sized by each ray's cone, and light bounced off snow carries its glints.
features.title: Snow

features.name: Histogram metering
features.what: lamps in view no longer darken the scene.
features.title: Exposure

features.name: Dark-scene key
features.what: night stays night.
features.title: Exposure

features.name: Pixel antialiasing
features.what: when Ray Reconstruction is off: samples after the first spread over the pixel (R2 sequence), so sub-pixel detail antialiases instead of sparkling.
features.title: DLSS Ray Reconstruction

features.name: Cloth tearing
features.what: overstretched edges split and the rip runs.
features.title: Physics (PhysX 5)

features.name: Camera-relative tracing
features.what: exact shadows and reflections far from the origin.
features.title: Open worlds

features.name: Persistent instances
features.what: unchanged objects and MultiMeshes cost no per-frame work.
features.title: Open worlds

features.name: Off-screen culling
features.what: small or distant unseen objects leave the trace.
features.title: Open worlds

features.name: Opacity micromaps
features.what: cut-out foliage traced without any-hit shaders.
features.title: Open worlds

features.name: Mesh LOD in the path tracer
features.title: Open worlds
